pairs.difference: A: the yellow background stays a solid mid-light value with a soft white pool around the whistle, and the whistle has big calm light and mid planes. The pattern icons read only faintly. B: the whole background is blown out to near-white, with a white halo hugging the outline. Only the icons hold any grey. The key is far higher than any real card (compare the calculator's yellow). The hero is the darkest mass by a wide margin, and a hard black-red wedge sits in the top window.
pairs.fix: Keep the background a deep, rich golden yellow, not pale. Remove the white halo around the whistle. Make the inside of the window a soft dark orange, not near-black red.

pairs.difference: A: the background rays stay in two close mid-light values, with only a small bright burst at the centre behind the coil. The rope is one compact dark shape. B: a broad glowing core spreads around the hero and the rays are stronger in the corners. The hero is ringed by the light. The bell has stacked hard-edged steps from white to dark, with a hard white rim line. The big tassels are heavy dark blobs with stepped facets.
pairs.fix: Dim the glow behind the bugle so the rays stay a soft, even turquoise. Shade the bell with one smooth gradient and a single soft highlight. Make the tassels small and slim.

pairs.difference: A: a bright orange glow sits directly behind the cup and floor, with dark corners, so the background splits into a hot halo and a mid floor. The cup breaks into many grey and white patches, and the flower is a heavy mid-grey shape. B: the background is one calm dark group with a soft vignette. The cup is one large light shape with a few quiet shadows, and the only deep accent is the contact shadow under the saucer.
pairs.fix: Remove the orange glow behind the cup and make the background a single dark red that falls off gently to the corners. Light the cup as one big soft white shape, with fewer shadow patches.

pairs.difference: A: the background is a light wall that falls to mid on the right, and the apples form one dark mass with soft round highlights. The shadow on the table is pale and soft. B: a light halo follows the handle and basket like a cut-out against the darker wall. The floor is flat near-white, the cast shadow is a hard-edged dark shape on the left, and the leaves add hard light flecks on the dark apple mass.
pairs.fix: Remove the glow behind the basket and let the wall darken gently toward one side only. Make the shadow on the table pale and soft-edged. Keep the apples one dark group, without bright leaves on top.

pairs.difference: A: the barrel is lit evenly from the front, with mid-grey staves and bands of similar value and no large light-to-dark division. Many small light and dark notes repeat on the rivets, and the only deep black sits in the top opening. B: the barrel splits into one large dark group on the left and a light group on the right. The bands follow the same fall-off, and the deep darks sit under the barrel and at the deck edge, as in the real camera lesson.
pairs.fix: Light the barrel from one side so its left half falls into one big dark shape and its right half stays light. Remove the shiny highlights on each rivet. Add a deep shadow under the barrel.

pairs.difference: A: the car body is one big white shape with quiet grey, and the darkest accents are the shadow under the car and the wipers and windscreen frame. The rays sit at mid value. B: the rays are brighter and glow behind the car. The body is broken up by hard white flecks, and the chrome bumper, grille and wheels have tightly stacked white-to-black steps. Glass highlights and interior darks add many small accents that compete all over the hero.
pairs.fix: Make the car one large calm yellow shape with soft shading. Use matte grey, not shiny chrome, on the bumper and grille. Darken the sky rays and remove the glow behind the car.

pairs.difference: A: the card reads as big groups: dark tree masses in the corners, a large mid-value tent and pale grass. There is one black accent at the door, so the eye lands there. B: light and dark are scattered evenly across the card, with leaves, flowers, ropes, stones and the lantern all carrying their own bright and dark flecks. The tent has no clear value separation from the busy ground, and no single darkest area dominates.
pairs.fix: Group the forest into a few large dark shapes and simplify the grass into one calm light area. Remove the flowers and small props. Keep the only near-black area inside the tent doorway.

pairs.difference: A: a dark overall key, with forest and frame merged into one large dark group. The pot is a big dark shape, the rim is a single light ring, and the small fire is the one bright spot. B: a higher, mid-light key, with light and dark notes distributed over logs, ropes, stones, crate, stump and stew. The stones and fire make a busy bright cluster at the bottom, and the dark pot is the only large group.
pairs.fix: Darken the forest and ground so they merge into one big dark background. Reduce the stew, stones and logs to a few simple shapes with soft shading. Leave the fire as the single brightest spot.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away in three ways. They put a bright halo or glow right behind the hero, so the background is lifted into a high key and the hero looks cut out. They scatter hard, small light and dark accents evenly over the card, with stepped speculars on chrome, rims and props, where real cards hold large calm value groups and one main dark accent. And they light heroes evenly from the front with crisp edges, where real cards let big areas fall into shadow and use soft cast shadows.
